title: Inverse-image compatibility of prescribed normalized Cech comparisons
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $X,Y$ schemes [def-pc-scheme], $g:Y\to X$, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $f^{\prime}:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. Let $U,V$ be open covers indexed by the same set $I$, with $V_{i_0\ldots i_k}\subseteq g^{-1}U_{i_0\ldots i_k}$ for every nonempty tuple. Let $M,N$ be arbitrary module sheaves, not necessarily quasi-coherent, and $\varphi:M\to g_*N$. For every pair of normalized additive comparison systems $c,c^{\prime}$ [def-pc-cech-comparison-system], for every degree $q$ and cycles $z,z^{\prime}$ in the scalar-restricted Cech complexes [lem-pc-flat-cech-base-change] whose coordinates match via $\varphi$ and restriction, $c^{\prime}_{f^{\prime}}([z^{\prime}])=H(\operatorname{coeff}(g,\varphi))(H(\operatorname{invImage}g,\operatorname{constIso}(g)^{-1})(c_f([z])))$, with Ext maps as in [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. No affine-intersection, quasi-coherence, scalar compatibility or bijectivity assertion is included.

source.place: Lemma 20.15.1, augmented pentagon and global-section squares; uniqueness of normalized comparisons by relative Cech effacement

proof.text: First identify any normalized system with the augmented-resolution comparison. The Cech cohomology functors are effaceable for the exact structure of coefficient sequences surjective on every tuple intersection: embed a sheaf F into the product of direct images of F restricted to each covering open. On any tuple intersection this embedding splits, using one member of that tuple, so the quotient sequence is admissible. The positive Cech cohomology of the product vanishes: in each factor insertion of its distinguished covering member contracts the Cech complex. Products of abelian groups are exact. Dimension shifting along these admissible sequences, naturality, and the connecting law show by induction that a normalized comparison is uniquely determined by its degree-zero law.

Now compute with the resolution comparisons. Resolve the source and target abelian sheaves and the pushed-forward target resolution. Lift the coefficient morphism and form the augmented pentagon of Tag 01FD. Tuple restriction commutes with the resolution maps and makes the two global-section squares commute. The coordinate hypothesis identifies the two coefficient-augmentation images of the cycles. Take total cohomology and invert the section-augmentation quasi-isomorphisms; the outer square gives equality of their comparison classes. Its action on sheaf cohomology is the displayed Ext action: inverse image is exact, sends the constant integer sheaf to itself via constIso, and the adjoint coefficient map is coeff. The derived section map and this Ext map agree in degree zero and commute with boundaries, hence agree in all degrees by effaceability of sheaf cohomology. Finally transport from module-valued to abelian Cech homology through the explicit scalar-restriction isomorphisms; these are coordinatewise identities. The uniqueness proved above substitutes the supplied systems for the resolution systems. In degree zero the diagram is gluing; an empty cover forces the scheme empty and the relevant groups zero. No acyclicity or quasi-coherence is used.

theorem cechComparison_inverseImage_compatibility
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u}
    (g : Y ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (f' : Y ⟶ Spec (.of S))
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (V : ι → Y.Opens) (hcover : iSup U = ⊤)
    (hcover' : iSup V = ⊤) (M : X.Modules) (N : Y.Modules)
    (φ : M ⟶ (pushforward g).obj N)
    (hinter : ∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin (k + 1) → ι),
      (⨅ l, V (y l)) ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ (⨅ l, U (y l)))
    (c : CechComparisonSystem U hcover) (c' : CechComparisonSystem V hcover') :
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (z : (cechOver f U M).cycles q) (z' : (cechOver f' V N).cycles q),
      (∀ y : Fin (q + 1) → ι,
        cechCoordinate f' V N q y ((cechOver f' V N).iCycles q z') =
          N.presheaf.map (homOfLE (hinter q y)).op
            (φ.val.app (op (⨅ l, U (y l)))
              (cechCoordinate f U M q y ((cechOver f U M).iCycles q z)))) →
      c'.overMap f' N q ((cechOver f' V N).homologyπ q z') =
        Sheaf.H.map (coeff g φ) q
          (Sheaf.H.mapFunctor (invImage g) (constIso g).symm
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.ringCatSheaf).obj M) q
              (c.overMap f M q ((cechOver f U M).homologyπ q z)))
